question_en: We cannot pay until Saturday; we will pay the total debt next week, plus 10% on top. Is that acceptable?
answer_exact: I was quite surprised to receive such last-minute notice, especially considering the mass email that I assume you sent to all the companies you've booked with. We have requested payment on several occasions, and you've assured us that it was being processed. As an alternative solution, we would prefer to receive payment directly from the guests and then reimburse them for any payments they've made to you. Let me know as soon as possible, as we will not be able to allow guest embarkation without the payment being settled.

question_en: Can we (the broker) cover the security deposit instead of the client, via payment link or by giving you our credit card?
answer_exact: As I have informed your colleague, we will not be able to accept the security deposit by your side. (Later, 2025-04-29:) The security deposit is secured through a pre-authorization on a credit or debit card, which is processed on the day of embarkation. This means that the specified amount is temporarily held (not charged) on the card to cover any potential damages or losses during the charter. In order to complete this transaction, the cardholder must be physically present at the base on the embarkation day. The cardholder is required to sign the pre-authorization slip, as per banking and security regulations. We cannot proceed with this step remotely or accept third-party authorization. (2025-07-03:) The security deposit should normally be withheld from the guests' card.
